messages.subject: Placement of CSS rules.
parts:
How are others adding rules to either their own css classes and ids or
those that are provided by shiny?

My answer is to override the headerPanel function with something like
this:

customHeaderPanel <- function(title,windowTitle=title){
tagList(
tags$head(
tags$title(windowTitle),
tags$link(rel="stylesheet", type="text/css",
href="app.css")
),
div(class = "span12", style = "padding: 10px 0px;", h1(title))
)
}

It's almost a verbatim copy of the headerPanel function but with the
added stylesheet link to my app's www/app.css file. I hate that I have
to override headerPanel, though.

I've got it working at:

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/jeffreyhorner/PowerSample/

and source code here:

https://github.com/jeffreyhorner/PowerSample

You can actually add <head> content from anywhere in the document, by
using tags$head, and Shiny will hoist them up to the correct place in
the final document. This doesn't work with HTML() literals or
reactiveUI, so watch out for those.

messages.subject: Re: Placement of CSS rules.
parts:
(Sorry if this is a dupe, I tried to send before but it didn't seem to go through)

You can actually put tags$head anywhere in the document and Shiny will hoist its contents up to the main <head> in the final document. No need to override headerPanel, you can just put it in the sidebar, or main panel, or whatever. Just note that this same behavior doesn't occur with HTML(), includeHTML, or reactiveUI/uiOutput.

parts:
It actually makes more sense to me if headerPanel were to gain the ... argument, as this reads well:

   # Application title
   headerPanel(
      "Power and Sample Size with spower from Hmisc",

and headerPanel could be written:

headerPanel <- function(title, ...){
  tagList(
    tags$head(tags$title(title),...),
    div(class="span12", style="padding: 10px 0px;",
      h1(title)
    )
  )
}

Of course this eliminates windowTitle from the argument list, but why would you need both anyway?

messages.subject: Re: Placement of CSS rules.
parts: windowTitle is needed in case you have HTML in the title, such as <em>, so those tags don't show up escaped in the browser window (tab) title. However we could do (title, ..., windowTitle), right? So you'd be forced to give a name to windowTitle? That's a breaking change but I bet there is only one person who has used that feature so far and we have his e-mail. :)
